title: Pendulum: damping not confirmed, so the agent asks for a bigger swing
description: A 0.5 m pendulum swinging for 6.5 s. Linear damping fits the whole swing slightly better, but forecasts the held-out quarter worse than the simple pendulum (13.8% against 9.9%), so verification does not pick it: the two laws tie. Both give g = 9.91 ± 0.04 m/s², 1% above 9.81 (the length is the uploader's stated 0.5 m), so g is measured either way. The agent designs the recording that would decide: release from about 35 degrees and film 7 s, where the two forecasts separate by 24 mm against 2.9 mm of tracking noise.
credit: Video: Rhetos / Mathe-AC Lernwerkstatt, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 (trimmed and downscaled)

truth.name: g
truth.source: standard gravity at the filming site (Aachen, 9.811 m/s^2); string length 0.5 m given
